messages.subject: frequency of concordance hits
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Can anyone think of a script for extracting only some concordance
hits?
For instance, each 4th hit of a word in a corpus.
I know MonoConc has this option in its search options, but I prefer
having the control I have with R.

Thanks,
Elitzur

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] frequency of concordance hits
messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] frequency of concordance hits
messages.body_plain:
Are the data too big to just generate all concordance lines and take a
random sample from them? As in:

#####
concordance.lines <- letters[1:20] # i.e., you have 20 concordance lines

# way 1:
set.seed(1) # make random numbers replicable
sampler <- sample(20) # random order of 1:20
your.sample.of.4.lines <- concordance.lines[sampler[1:4]]

# way 2:
your.sample.of.4.lines <- concordance.lines[floor(seq(1, 20, length.out=4))]

And as usual, there are many other ways ...

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara

messages.subject: Odd problem with pasting script into R
messages.subject_clean: Odd problem with pasting script into R
messages.body_plain:
This isn't directly an R concern so I'm not too optimistic that anyone here can help me, but it does involve R so here goes.

I have a good-sized R program I'm trying to run. It's scripted in gedit (so, Linux), but when I paste it into a terminal running R, some lines get truncated in the process, resulting in errors. But they *are* in the gedit file, and if I paste them one by one they work. Some lines that are exactly the same length or longer are pasted no problem.

Odder still, sometimes when it is processing a loop and the output is inanimate, I can look at the script in the terminal, I can sometimes see characters that shouldn't be there. For example, the last two lines of something currently running is:
+ }
n
That n shouldn't be there. It's not even the next character (and whenever I run this script, it's a different character in that spot). I can also see another random character higher up on the screen. I made certain I didn't hit the keyboard after pasting. (Hopefully they don't spell out 'Satan' or anything...) However, I'm not sure this is related or not because, unlike the truncated lines, these characters don't seem to get processed.

Any ideas what could be causing this? This is being done on a newish laptop, running Mint 10 Julia.

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D, ACS, ALB
Korea Maritime University
Lt Governor of Education & Training, Korea Territorial Council (Toastmasters)
Schoolmasters: http://grou.ps/schoolmasters/
National Korea Toastmasters: http://grou.ps/koreatoastmasters
